decision: The exact-order repair survives the zero-GPU gate for one later director-nominated H200 exact-consumer component falsifier. No performance magnitude transfers from the rejected source.

causal_localization.stock: 672 threads, contiguous BF16 vec8 mapping, one local round, XOR warp reduction, then XOR across 21 warp sums
causal_localization.rejected: 256 threads, scalar stride-256 mapping with 21 sequential values per thread, down-shuffle warp reduction, then down-shuffle across 8 warp sums

m1.deterministic_loaded_weight_case: square_sum differs in 1/1 row but BF16 normalized, scale, and activation bytes reconverge
m1.interpretation: The operation order already diverges at square_sum; this row does not cross a later rounding boundary.

m16.interpretation: The first possible semantic divergence is square_sum, before BF16 normalization and quantization; measured H200 rows prove later boundary crossings occur.

corrected_candidate.fallback: stock for M>32, non-BF16, non-2D, hidden size !=5376, or residual-bearing norm calls

physical_falsifier.later_reject_rule: Reject on any M=1/16/32 activation, scale, or consumer byte mismatch; graph/path/resource failure; incomplete ledger; or non-positive contemporaneous M32 real-QKV component median.

next_action: Director may nominate exactly one H200 M=1/16/32 real-QKV component run of the corrected source under a new positive-spend binding. Require exact activation, scale, and consumer bytes plus graph/path/resource proof before interpreting timing.
